brief.headline: Push for 60-day payment terms (worth ₹5.36 L cash freed up) and ask them to match a maker's price — they're 100% a trader, so we're paying their reseller margin.

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match a manufacturer's price or cut their margin — they don't make anything, they resell, so we're paying extra for that.
priceAsk.target: Benchmark to ₹0.65–0.80/pc for caps (market research shows this is achievable at higher volume) vs the typical reseller ask of ₹0.85–0.95/pc
priceAsk.basis: Their revenue mix is 100.0% traded, 0.0% manufactured — they buy from a maker and mark it up. We should pay closer to what the maker charges, not a middle-man price. Market research shows caps can go to ₹0.65–0.80/pc at volume, and the typical reseller band is ₹0.85–0.95/pc — we want the maker-level price.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days to 60 days after receipt — they already take 105 days to pay their own suppliers, so asking for 60 is only fair.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: This frees up ₹5.36 L in cash for us (and another ₹2.68 L if we stretch to 45 days).

brief.financialLeverage: They're a small, fragile supplier — revenue ₹54.69 Cr, money-health score 2/10, and in the grey zone (Altman Z 1.58), which means some distress risk. We're 1.19% of their sales, so a meaningful customer. They keep only 2.8% profit on every sale (similar firms keep 3.1%), so a big price cut could tip them over. But they take 105 days to pay their own suppliers (vs 57 days for peers) and collect in just 48 days, so their cash cycle is only 1 day — tighter than most (59 days). They can afford to wait longer for our payment. Lead with payment terms and the trader-margin issue; don't squeeze price so hard you break them.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms. Much stronger and a direct fit for our packaging needs.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed, profitable rigid-plastic leader (pails, containers, pharma) — a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: IVL Dhunseri Petrochem Industries Private Limited
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ): manufacturer in India-East, medium confidence — potential direct maker source to cut out the trader margin.

risks: Their money-health is weak (2/10, C rating, grey distress zone) — don't put all our eggs in this basket; line up Manjushree or another alternate now.
They have pending legal case(s) — check what those are before we rely on them for critical supply.
They keep only 2.8% profit per sale — pushing price too hard could push them into the red and hurt our supply; win more on payment terms.
They're 100% a trader — if we find the actual maker (one of the market backup leads like IVL Dhunseri or Reliance), we can bypass them entirely and save the reseller margin.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to move to 60-day payment terms — you already take 105 days to pay your own suppliers, so this is fair — and we need to talk about pricing, because you're reselling and we'd like to get closer to what the manufacturer charges.
